patch_description: The current algorithm sends every partition of a destination along the exact same single shortest path, causing all partitions to redundantly traverse the same (potentially expensive) links and concentrate load on one route. A better strategy: (1) compute k-shortest simple paths per destination using Yen's algorithm, (2) select a diverse set of paths — cycling through the k candidates so partitions are spread across parallel routes/networks, reducing per-link congestion and leveraging multi-network topologies, and (3) reweigh edges dynamically by adding a congestion penalty proportional to how many partitions already used that edge, which balances load across networks. If k-shortest paths fail for some destination, fall back to Dijkstra. This reduces redundant transfers, spreads cost across cheaper parallel links, and exploits multiple egress routes to minimize total transfer cost.
